answer: Use herbarium collection record with specimen accession history as the proof: specimens accessioned at one herbarium for years. One fake is cheap, but 532 aliases need 532 independent accession histories, and the time invested in each is the price the farm pays. Each epoch demands a fresh attestation from the issuer, and stale or copied records fail the check. The copper check runs in the open: 532 fakes pay the full price 532 times, one honest agent pays once, and the crystal trail in the ledger makes the zephyr cost visible to everyone.
